theme: The Shema; love and memory; do not forget God
readingInstruction: Read Deuteronomy 6:1-8:20. This is the heart of the book. It contains the Shema, the greatest commandment, and Moses’ warnings about forgetting God in prosperity. Read chapter 6 slowly, and think about verses 4 to 9 as the center.
settingTheScene: Moses now moves from the Ten Commandments to their meaning. These chapters begin with the greatest commandment and then apply it to life in the land. They deal with passing faith to the next generation, the dangers of prosperity, and the testing in the wilderness. The Shema, the opening words of 6:4, are recited by Jewish people daily to this day.
observation: “Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one” (6:4).
“You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might” (6:5).
“And these words that I command you today shall be on your heart” (6:6).
“You shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise” (6:7).
“When your son asks you in time to come, What is the meaning of the testimonies… then you shall say to your son, We were Pharaoh’s slaves in Egypt” (6:20-21).
The LORD did not set his love on Israel because they were more in number, but “because the LORD loves you and is keeping the oath that he swore to your fathers” (7:7-8).
“And you shall remember the whole way that the LORD your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, that he might humble you, testing you” (8:2).
“Man does not live by bread alone, but man lives by every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD” (8:3).
interpretation:
The Shema is the center of Israel’s faith, and of the Bible’s teaching about God. “The LORD our God, the LORD is one.” There is one God, and he is the covenant God. The statement is both theological and personal. He is “our God.” And the response to him is not just assent but love, with the whole person: heart, soul, and might.

Moses ties love to obedience, and obedience to teaching. The words are to be on the heart first, before they are taught to the children. A parent cannot pass on what he does not hold. And the teaching is to happen in all of ordinary life: at home, on the road, at bedtime, at waking. It is not a classroom subject. It is the atmosphere of the household. The signs on the hand and forehead and doorposts are reminders that faith belongs to every part of life.

Then comes a warning about success. “When the LORD your God brings you into the land… take care lest you forget the LORD.” The danger is not hardship but plenty. In good times, we easily imagine that we have earned what we have. Moses says, “You shall remember the LORD your God, for it is he who gives you power to get wealth” (8:18).

Chapter 7 gives a stunning reason for God’s choice of Israel. It was not their size or strength. “The LORD set his love on you” because he loved you. There is no explanation behind love except love itself. This is grace in the Old Testament.

The wilderness years, according to chapter 8, were not wasted. God humbled and tested them to teach one lesson: “Man does not live by bread alone.” Jesus quoted it when tempted in the desert. The manna was a lesson in daily dependence. The forty years were a school of trust.
connection: Jesus calls the Shema “the great and first commandment” (Matthew 22:36-38), and he quotes Deuteronomy 8:3 against Satan (Matthew 4:4). Paul says that “there is one God, the Father… and one Lord, Jesus Christ” (1 Corinthians 8:6), and John says that God’s love for us was shown when “he sent his Son” (1 John 4:10). Ephesians 6:4 tells fathers to bring up their children “in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.”
application:
Say the Shema aloud, slowly. Ask what it would mean to love God with every part of you.

Think of one concrete way you can bring God’s word into the ordinary rhythms of your home this week.

Ask whether prosperity or comfort has dulled your dependence on God.
prayerPrompts: Tell God you want to love him with all your heart, soul, and might, and where that is hard.
Ask him to keep you from forgetting him in good times.
Ask him to help you teach his words to someone else.
